leakage_policy: Each record is quantized only from its current K and V tensors; dense AV is evaluation-only.
Validation and test records do not select bit width, stage count, block size, exact frames, or centroids.
K-means is per-record and training-free, matching runtime-observable QVG semantics rather than fitting a held-out codebook.
Captured K is post-RoPE; the probe deterministically removes captured 3D RoPE, quantizes canonical K, and restores the original per-token RoPE before attention.
The saved queries cover four 64-token tiles per query frame, so AV fidelity is a sampled-query result, not a full-grid rollout result.
decision_rules: If the primary INT2 method fails either AV quality gate, do not build query-selective residual decoding on this representation.
If quality passes but compression is below 6x, retain QVG only as a baseline and inspect metadata overhead before extending it.
A passing cache result supports a memory direction only; it does not support an attention or end-to-end speedup claim.
Only after the primary method passes may a separate frozen protocol test centroid-only, partial-residual, and exact-token refinement for compute reduction.
Because a 12-frame cache makes exact sink/recent storage expensive, that arm is a quality sensitivity test rather than the primary compression claim.
